hazard: Lack of approved mental health practitioner for assessment
theme: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

reports.title: Richard Carlon
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

promises.quote: West Midlands Police will ensure any caller is updated when a missing person has been located to allow further contact between parties. This may not always mean full details of whereabouts are disclosed (as individual cases may prevent this from being appropriate) however, the reasons for this will be recorded and explained in each case.
promises.summary: Update callers when missing persons are located

concerns.quote: No approved Mental Health practitioner was available to make the Mental Health Act assessment of Mr Carlon on 14/11/18. I was told this was an ongoing problem and was delaying assessments.
concerns.hazard: lack of approved mental health practitioner for assessment

concerns.quote: When Mr Carlon was found safe and well at home WMP did not advise BSMHT. This was a missed opportunity for Mental health to re‐engage with Mr Carlon and make a further assessment of his condition. Consideration need to be given to how agencies can improve communication.
concerns.hazard: failure to notify mental health team after safe check

reports.title: Parminder Sanghera: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

concerns.quote: During the course of the inquest, I heard evidence Mr Sanghera was deemed to be suffering from behavioural issues rather than a mental health crisis and no full Mental Health Act assessment took place either at New Cross Hospital or whilst in custody at Oldbury Police station.
concerns.hazard: lack of full mental health act assessment before release

links.explanation: Both reports highlight failures to conduct a proper Mental Health Act assessment when individuals were experiencing a mental health crisis. The earlier case cites unavailability of approved practitioners, while the later case notes misclassification of behaviour preventing assessment.
